extra.message: User input from request.GET.get('host') is concatenated directly into a shell command string passed to os.system(). An attacker can inject arbitrary shell commands (e.g., '; rm -rf /').

User input from request.GET.get('expr') is passed directly to eval(). Although __builtins__ is set to empty dict, sandbox escapes exist (e.g., via ().__class__.__bases__[0].__subclasses__()), allowing arbitrary Python code execution.
User-controlled data from request.body or request.GET.get('blob') is deserialized with pickle.loads(). pickle deserialization on untrusted data allows arbitrary code execution.

User input from request.GET.get('name') is used directly in a path join (BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name) without sanitization. The file is written with request.body content. This allows path traversal to write arbitrary files anywhere on the filesystem.

User-controlled JSON from request.body is decoded and passed directly as a MongoDB query to find_one() without sanitization. Attackers can inject MongoDB operators (e.g., {'$gt': ''}) to bypass authentication or extract data.

lxml XML parser is configured with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, and no_network=False, enabling XML External Entity (XXE) processing. User-supplied XML in request.body can read local files or perform SSRF.

User input from request.GET.get('lane') or request.POST.get('lane') is passed directly to django.shortcuts.redirect() without validation. An attacker can craft a URL that redirects users to a malicious site.
The full request body and Authorization header value are logged at WARNING level via logger.warning(). This exposes sensitive credentials and request payloads in log files.

extra.message: Exception details including internal filesystem path (BASE_EXPORT_DIR) and exception class name are returned in the HTTP 500 response body, leaking internal infrastructure information to clients.

extra.message: Access-Control-Allow-Origin is set to a user-supplied origin value (from request.headers.get('origin')) while Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is set to true. This allows any malicious site to make credentialed cross-origin requests, leading to CSRF-like attacks.

extra.message: The case_matter_file_048 endpoint has no authentication check (no call to _wrk_gate) and is publicly accessible. It exposes operational data including case counts and sensitive metadata to unauthenticated users.

extra.message: The client_edit view only checks if the user has a staff role but does not verify whether the user is authorized to access the specific client identified by pk. Any staff member can edit any client's profile regardless of whether they work with that client.

extra.message: Django SECRET_KEY falls back to the hardcoded string 'dev-only-change-me' if the DJANGO_SECRET_KEY environment variable is not set. This weakens cryptographic signing and session security.

DEBUG is enabled by default (falls back to '1' if DJANGO_DEBUG is not set). Debug mode exposes stack traces, SQL queries, and configuration details to users, enabling information gathering for attacks.
Security headers X-XSS-Protection and Content-Security-Policy are explicitly disabled (set to '0' and '' respectively), removing browser-side XSS and content injection protections.
Verification values (handle-to-code mapping: 'north':'4812', 'south':'5930') are hardcoded in the source code rather than stored in a secure configuration or database.
SSL certificate verification is disabled via ssl._create_unverified_context() for an outbound HTTPS request. This enables man-in-the-middle attacks when connecting to the partner endpoint.
